## ROOT repair directive — angle 0 v2

**Decision: REVISE, not terminal.** The product-scale lower-bound kernel remains viable, but the flagship experiment must be replaced with Gu–Yin–Cai–Fan’s exact fixed-class experiment. Do not try to rescue the present “observed-code minimax frontier” comparison through prose. A bridge would be a separate, substantial theorem and is unavailable in the current proposal.

### 1. Replace the risk and its quantifiers

Delete `Γ_n(b_n)`, `R_n(b_n)`, the code spaces, code variables, jointly measurable decoding machinery, `def:observed-code-minimax-risk`, and every “observed-code” or “common-code” headline.

Reproduce Gu et al.’s objects faithfully:

\[
\mathcal T_3=\{f\in L^2(\nu_d):\|f\|_\infty\le3\},
\]

\[
\mathcal H_n(\bar\delta)=
\left\{
F\subseteq\mathcal T_3:
\exists G\subseteq\mathcal T_3,\
\sup_{f\in F}\inf_{g\in G}\|f-g\|_{L^2(\nu_d)}
\le\delta^{\rm appr},\
\sup_{\delta\ge\delta^{\rm stoc}}
\frac{\mathcal R_{n,\nu_d}(\delta;\partial G)}{3\delta}
\le\delta^{\rm stoc}
\right\}.
\]

Distinguish the **truth class** \(F\) from its **learner-class witness** \(G\); the current artifact incorrectly replaces Gu’s uniform truth-class condition by an instancewise condition on \(P\).

Define the exact Appendix A.1 family

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal P_{\rm Gu}(F_\mu,F_\pi)=\{P_{\beta,v,\mu,\pi}:&
\ X\sim\nu_d,\quad \mu\in F_\mu,\quad \pi\in F_\pi,\\
&T=\pi(X)+u,\quad E[u\mid X]=0,\quad
E[u^2\mid X]\equiv v\ge1/3,\\
&Y=\beta T+\mu(X)+\varepsilon,\quad
E[\varepsilon\mid X,T]=0,\\
&|\beta|\vee|v|\le3,\quad |T|\vee|Y|\le3\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Then use Gu’s quantifier order exactly:

\[
m_{\rm Gu}(n,\bar\delta_\mu,\bar\delta_\pi)
=
\sup_{F_\mu\in\mathcal H_n(\bar\delta_\mu)}
\sup_{F_\pi\in\mathcal H_n(\bar\delta_\pi)}
\inf_{\widehat\beta}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\rm Gu}(F_\mu,F_\pi)}
E_{P^{\otimes 2n}}|\widehat\beta-\beta(P)|.
\]

The infimum occurs **after** the fixed class pair is selected. Thus \(\widehat\beta\) may be tailored to and know \(F_\mu,F_\pi\), their learner witnesses, and the budgets. Gu’s outer supremum is not a random or hidden class choice.

Gu Appendix A.1 explicitly uses this fixed-class order and a \(2n\)-sample risk; its upper bound therefore applies to this \(m_{\rm Gu}\), not to the current jointly measurable observed-code risk. [Gu et al., Appendix A.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.06368v1)

### 2. Use this as the sole flagship statement

Replace the open-ended question by the following minimal formal statement:

> For every budget sequence
> \[
> \bar\delta_{\mu,n}=(0,s_{\mu,n}),\qquad
> \bar\delta_{\pi,n}=(0,s_{\pi,n})
> \]
> satisfying
> \[
> n^{-1/2}\le s_{\pi,n}=o(s_{\mu,n}),\qquad
> s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n}\to0,\qquad
> n^{-1/2}=o(s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n}),
> \]
> is
> \[
> m_{\rm Gu}(n,\bar\delta_{\mu,n},\bar\delta_{\pi,n})
> \gtrsim s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n}?
> \]

State the constructive quantifiers explicitly in the proof handle:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\forall (s_{\mu,n},s_{\pi,n})\text{ in the regime},\
\exists c>0,N,\
\forall n\ge N,\
\exists F_{\mu,n}\in\mathcal H_n(0,s_{\mu,n}),\
\exists F_{\pi,n}\in\mathcal H_n(0,s_{\pi,n})\\
\text{such that}\quad
\inf_{\widehat\beta_n}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\rm Gu}(F_{\mu,n},F_{\pi,n})}
E_{P^{\otimes2n}}|\widehat\beta_n-\beta(P)|
\ge c\,s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n}.
\end{aligned}
\]

This is the correct fixed-pair witness statement. Both fuzzy hypotheses must be supported on the same nonrandom \(F_{\mu,n},F_{\pi,n}\), every mixture component must satisfy Gu’s exact (A.1) family, and affinity must be computed after \(2n\) i.i.d. observations. The class pair may depend on \(n\) and the budgets but cannot depend on the hypothesis or estimator.

To preserve the proposal’s claimed continuous-treatment niche, require the hard witness distributions additionally to have **bounded non-atomic treatment laws**. This is a restriction of \(\mathcal P_{\rm Gu}\), so a lower bound on that subclass still lower-bounds \(m_{\rm Gu}\), while preventing the result from being a repackaging of the existing binary-treatment theorem.

### 3. Do not pursue the observed-code bridge in this revision

The generic minimax inequality goes in the unhelpful direction:

\[
\inf_{\delta(\text{class},D)}\sup_{\text{class}}\sup_P R
\ \ge\
\sup_{\text{class}}\inf_{\delta_{\text{class}}}\sup_P R.
\]

Consequently, Gu’s upper bound for the right-hand fixed-class risk does not upper-bound the broader observed-code risk. A valid bridge would need, at minimum, a uniform jointly measurable selection theorem producing class-tailored estimators with Gu’s rate over the entire coded class universe, plus an exact identification of the coded families with \(\mathcal H_n\). That is new mathematics, may fail for arbitrary standard-Borel codings, and distracts from the product-converse kernel. Replace the broader risk rather than asserting this bridge.

The causal potential-outcome layer may be retained only as an optional lemma showing that the constructed hard subclass admits a constant-effect causal extension. It must not redefine or narrow the headline comparator silently.

### 4. Preserve the strictness calculation

Keep the asymmetric algebra, now stated for \(m_{\rm Gu}\). With zero approximation budgets,

\[
U_n=n^{-1/2}+\min\{s_{\mu,n}^2,\ s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n}\}
\asymp s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n},
\]

whereas Gu’s displayed lower expression is

\[
L_n=n^{-1/2}+s_{\mu,n}^2s_{\pi,n}^2+s_{\pi,n}^2
=o(s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n}).
\]

Therefore an affirmative result is genuinely a strict improvement of Gu’s displayed lower bound and, on the same experiment, closes the gap to Gu’s upper bound. Do not say merely that the numerical expressions “match” while referring to another risk.

### 5. Add the precise Jin–Mackey–Syrgkanis comparison

Add a distinct bibliography entry:

> Jin, J., Mackey, L., and Syrgkanis, V. (2025). *It’s Hard to Be Normal: The Impact of Noise on Structure-agnostic Estimation*. NeurIPS 2025; arXiv:2507.02275.

Do not conflate it with `jin2025sharp`, the separate Jin–Syrgkanis paper on general linear functionals.

The related-work comparison must say:

> Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis study PLM-coefficient estimation given fixed black-box estimates \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\) of \(g_0=E[T\mid X]\) and \(q_0=E[Y\mid X]\), with local \(L^s(P)\) error radii \((\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)\), and use worst-case quantile minimax error. Their Theorem 3.1 proves, for bounded binary treatment with overlap and uniform covariates, a lower bound of order
> \[
> n^{-1/2}+\epsilon_1^2+\epsilon_1\epsilon_2
> \]
> up to fixed overlap constants. Their Theorem 3.2 proves for conditionally Gaussian treatment noise of known constant variance a product lower bound
> \[
> n^{-1/2}+\epsilon_1\epsilon_2
> \left\{\frac{\log(1/\epsilon_1)}{\log n}\right\}^{3}
> \]
> up to variance constants, matching DML when \(\epsilon_1\) is polynomial in \(n^{-1}\). They also show that independent non-Gaussian noise can permit higher-order ACE rates. These results do not prove the proposed theorem: they use local neighborhoods around supplied nuisance estimates, the nuisances \((g_0,q_0)\), and quantile loss, rather than Gu’s outer supremum over fixed truth classes with localized-critical-radius witnesses and expected absolute loss. Moreover, the proposed hard pair is required to use bounded non-atomic treatment, excluding their binary and Gaussian regimes.

These are the relevant theorem statements in the [NeurIPS paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.02275).

Retain Jin–Syrgkanis `jin2025sharp` only with the narrower description that its PLM-preserving example concerns expected conditional covariance and explicitly does not establish the present PLM-coefficient frontier.

The literal equation (A.1) really displays
\[
E[\varepsilon Y\mid X,T]=0,
\]
with \(Y\) multiplying \(\varepsilon\). It is not typeset as a subscript, the error is introduced as \(\varepsilon\), and no \(\varepsilon_Y\) notation is defined. The paper’s main model (1.1) and its earlier minimax family (3.2), however, both impose \(E[\varepsilon\mid X,T]=0\). Thus the extra \(Y\) is very likely a typographical error—not an \(\varepsilon_Y\) convention—but this cannot be silently corrected or quoted as the literal content of (A.1) without an author correction or erratum. [Gu–Yin–Cai–Fan, equations (1.1), (3.2), and (A.1)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.06368).

The literal condition is mathematically different. If
\[
a(X,T)=\beta T+\mu(X),\qquad Y=a+\varepsilon,
\]
then it says
\[
aE[\varepsilon\mid X,T]+E[\varepsilon^2\mid X,T]=0.
\]
Consequently, combining it with mean-zero error would force \(\varepsilon=0\) almost surely.

More decisively, the literal model destroys identification even in the proposed non-atomic subclass. Take
\[
F_\mu=F_\pi=G_\mu=G_\pi=\{0\},\quad
T=u\sim {\rm Unif}[-1,1],\quad v=1/3,\quad
Y=0,\quad \varepsilon=-\beta T .
\]
These singleton classes are admissible at every stated budget, \(T\) is bounded and non-atomic, and \(E[\varepsilon Y\mid X,T]=0\). Yet every \(\beta\in[-3,3]\) induces the same observed law. \[
\max_{\beta\in\{-3,3\}}E|\widehat\beta-\beta|\ge3.
\]
This contradicts Theorem A.1’s vanishing upper bound at zero budgets. Therefore the literal equation cannot consistently support the claimed fixed-class rate frontier.
